title: I built a dating game that runs through your existing ChatGPT subscription instead of charging you for another AI subscription
author: Machine-Federal
selftext:
I've been working on an AI dating game called **Where This Goes**, and one of the main design decisions was that I didn't want to build another AI product that requires its own monthly subscription.

So if someone already has ChatGPT, they can use that subscription to play the game.

But one thing I found pretty quickly was that letting the LLM handle everything doesn't work very well for an actual game.

The model handles the character dialogue, but the game keeps a separate structured state for things like:

* relationship progression
* memories and promises
* current scene and location
* outfits
* conflict / friction
* boundaries
* character state

That ended up being a much bigger part of development than the actual prompting.

For example, I had cases where a character would say they were going somewhere, but the visual scene wouldn't change. Or a relationship would suddenly feel much more intimate after only a couple of turns. Or something important from 20 turns ago would effectively disappear.

I've been moving more and more of that responsibility out of the model and into persistent game state, while still letting the model decide how the character actually talks and reacts.

The interesting part now is trying to find the line between too much deterministic game logic and giving the model enough freedom that conversations don't feel scripted.

The game currently supports ChatGPT, external models and local LLMs, so I'm also starting to see how differently models behave with the same relationship state.

I released the first version on itch today. It's still early, but I'm mostly interested in testing the architecture at this point rather than pretending it's a finished giant dating sim.

[https://choices-matter.itch.io/where-this-goes](https://choices-matter.itch.io/where-this-goes)

I'd be interested in how other people are handling persistent state in LLM games. Are you letting the model infer most of it, or explicitly tracking it outside the context?
